title: Resolution of complete normal local surfaces
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian normal local domain of Krull dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], complete for its maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. There exist an integral scheme $T$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] and a proper morphism $f:T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum] inducing an isomorphism of function fields [def-sc-function-field], such that $T$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0BGN, resolve-lemma-resolve-complete; resolution means a proper birational morphism with integral regular source, as in resolve-definition-resolution.

proof.text: By the complete-local finite-over-regular theorem, choose a complete regular local subring $R\subseteq A$ with $A$ finite over $R$. Write $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$. Finiteness makes the inclusion integral, hence $\dim R=\dim A=2$, and $n=[K:F]$ is finite and positive. Prove simultaneously, by strong induction on $n$, the following assertion: every finite inclusion $R\subseteq D$ of a complete regular local domain into a complete normal Noetherian local domain, both of dimension $2$, with $[\operatorname{Frac}D:\operatorname{Frac}R]=n$, admits a proper birational regular integral model of $\operatorname{Spec}D$. The chosen $R\subseteq A$ is one instance. The induction permits all complete regular bases, not only this initial $R$.

source.place: Tag 0BGN, initial choice of A_0 and induction on fraction-field degree.

proof.text: Fix an instance $R\subseteq A$ of degree $n$ and assume the induction assertion for all smaller positive degrees. The complete rings $R,A$ are excellent and Nagata. Every ring essentially of finite type over either is excellent by finite-type/localization stability, hence Nagata by quasi-excellent-implies-Nagata. We use these properties below on local rings of finite-type models. Regularity of $R$ at its maximal ideal implies regularity of all its localizations; regular-implies-normal applied to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ makes $R$ integrally closed in $F$. If $n=1$, identify $K=F$. Every element of $A$ is integral over $R$ and lies in $F$, so $A=R$. Its spectrum is regular, integral, and the identity is the required proper birational map: it is separated, finite type and remains a closed map under every base change, as in the definition of properness.

source.place: Tag 0BGN, opening excellency paragraph and degree-one base case.

proof.text: Suppose first that $F\subsetneq L\subsetneq K$. Put $B=A\cap L$. This equals the integral closure of $R$ in $L$: elements of $A$ are integral over $R$, and an element of $L$ integral over $R$ is integral over $A$ and hence belongs to $A$ by normality. Also $B$ is normal: an element of $\operatorname{Frac}B\subseteq L$ integral over $B$ is integral over $A$, so lies in $A\cap L$. Its fraction field is $L$: for $z\in L$ use its monic algebraic equation over $F$, and choose nonzero $r\in R$ clearing the coefficients; the equation for $rz$ has coefficients $r^ic_{m-i}\in R$, so $rz\in B$. As an $R$-submodule of finite $A$, the ring $B$ is finite. The finite-over-complete theorem makes this domain complete Noetherian local, and the integral-dimension theorem gives $\dim B=2$. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_A\cap B$, since the finite inclusions are local by the uniqueness clause of that theorem. The tower formula gives $[L:F]<n$ and $[K:L]<n$. Apply induction to $R\subseteq B$ to obtain an integral regular proper birational model $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$.

source.place: Tag 0BGN, intermediate-field paragraph: construction of B and first induction application.

proof.text: The finite-type model $Y$ is excellent, Noetherian, and has dimension $2$: it is a regular proper birational model over the excellent local surface $B$. The closed-dominant dimension theorem applies to its proper dominant finite-type structure map with trivial extension of function fields, and gives $\dim Y=\dim B=2$. Now normalize $Y$ in $K$ and call the result $X$. The normalization-cover lemma, with $C=B,D=A$, gives $X$ normal, integral, excellent and Noetherian of dimension $2$, and a proper birational $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. By the normal-surface local-data lemma its singular set is a finite set of closed points $x_i$ of local dimension $2$. At $y_i=\pi(x_i)$ the cover lemma gives a finite inclusion of complete local domains $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y,y_i}\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x_i}$, with regular base of dimension $2$, normal target of dimension $2$, and field degree at most $[K:L]<n$. Apply induction to each of these inclusions to resolve $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x_i}$.

source.place: Tag 0BGN, intermediate-field normalization and smaller completed local degrees.

proof.text: For each singular $x_i$, refine its completed-local resolution to a finite proper normalized point blowup tower by the normalized-refinement theorem. Descend that tower along $\mathcal O_{X,x_i}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x_i}$ using completion descent; the normal completion and local dimension $2$ are supplied by local data. The descended endpoint is regular. Globalize the finitely many towers on $X$ by local-normalized-blowup globalization. Outside the $x_i$ it is an isomorphism to a regular open. At a point over $x_i$, its local ring is the corresponding local ring of the regular local endpoint, by the globalization statement. Thus the global endpoint $T$ is regular. The normalized-tower geometry lemma makes $T$ integral and the tower projective and birational; projective-bundle properness makes it proper; composing with $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ preserves properness and the identity of function fields. This completes the intermediate-field induction case, including an empty singular set.

source.place: Tag 0BGN, intermediate-field paragraph: refinement, completion descent, and globalization.

proof.text: It remains to treat $n>1$ with no strict intermediate field. Let $K_s$ be the separable closure of $F$ in $K$. The separable-first theorem says that $K_s/F$ is separable and $K/K_s$ purely inseparable. Thus $K_s=K$, in which case $K/F$ is separable, or $K_s=F$, in which case $K/F$ is purely inseparable of positive characteristic $p$. In the latter case the degree-$p$ intermediate-step theorem gives $K/M$ of degree $p$ for some intermediate $M$; since $M\ne K$, absence of strict intermediates forces $M=F$, so $n=p$. In the separable case, the regular-surface-rational theorem gives rationality of $R$, hence bounded modification genus with bound zero, and separable ascent gives bounded modification genus for $A$. In the inseparable degree-$p$ case, $A$ is the integral closure of $R$ in $K$ (by the same integrality and normality argument as in Step 3); apply the degree-$p$ rational-reduction theorem. In both cases reduction to rational singularities is possible for $A$.

Apply the bounded-genus rational-model theorem to $A$. Obtain a finite tower of normalized point blowups $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ such that every closed local ring of dimension $2$ on $X$ is rational. The tower-geometry theorem gives $X$ integral, normal, Noetherian, excellent and of dimension $2$, with proper birational composite. By normal-surface local data, the singular set is finite, say $\{x_1,\ldots,x_t\}$, and each $R_i=\mathcal O_{X,x_i}$ is a normal excellent Nagata local domain of dimension $2$ with normal completion. It is rational by the rational-model conclusion, and it is essentially of finite type over the complete local ring $A$. Apply the rational-surface Gorenstein blowup theorem to each $R_i$. This gives finite ordinary point blowup towers with normal intermediate schemes and Gorenstein local rings at the endpoints.

Each ordinary tower just obtained is also a normalized tower: after each blowup its scheme is already normal, so the subsequent normalization is an isomorphism (the length-zero normal-open clause of tower geometry). Globalize these towers at $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ using local-normalized-blowup globalization, obtaining $X'\to X$. Its endpoint local rings above $x_i$ are those of the chosen Gorenstein endpoint. Off the $x_i$ the scheme is regular. The tower-geometry theorem gives $X'$ normal integral excellent Noetherian of dimension $2$. Its singular points $x'_j$ are finite and have dimension-two local rings by local data; each lies over an $x_i$, since the complement is unchanged and regular. Hence each $S_j=\mathcal O_{X',x'_j}$ is Gorenstein by the endpoint local-ring identification.

source.place: Tag 0BGN, globalization of the Gorenstein-producing towers, via Tag 0BFZ after the normal-intermediate observation.

proof.text: For each singular $x'_j$ over $x_i$, the local map $R_i\to S_j$ is injective, local, essentially of finite type and induces an isomorphism of fraction fields, because it is induced by the birational blowup tower. The rational-propagation theorem applies: $R_i$ is a rational normal Nagata local domain of dimension $2$; $S_j$ is normal and has dimension $2$. Thus $S_j$ is rational. Normal-surface local data gives its normal completion, and excellence gives the Nagata condition. Together with Step 8's Gorenstein property, these are exactly the hypotheses of the rational-double-point theorem. It gives a finite ordinary blowup tower at singular closed points over $\operatorname{Spec}S_j$, with normal intermediate schemes and regular endpoint.

source.place: Tag 0BGN, final rational-double-point paragraph, with rationality propagation Tag 0BG0 explicit.

proof.text: The ordinary towers of Step 9 are normalized towers because their intermediate schemes are normal, just as in Step 8. Globalize them at the finitely many singular $x'_j$ of $X'$. Call the endpoint $T$. For a point of $T$ whose image is not one of the $x'_j$, the morphism is an isomorphism to the regular complement. For a point over $x'_j$, globalization identifies its local ring with that of the regular endpoint chosen over $S_j$. Thus every local ring of $T$ is regular; $T$ is locally Noetherian by tower geometry, so $T$ is regular. Concatenating the three finite normalized towers and applying tower geometry over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ shows that $T$ is integral and $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is projective and induces an isomorphism of function fields; projective-bundle properness gives properness. This completes the remaining induction case. Strong induction and Step 1 therefore prove the item.

source.place: Tag 0BGN, final globalization and local-ring regularity check.

The item statement is unchanged and matches 0BGN with resolve-definition-resolution. Steps 1-10 follow the 0BGN route. Step 1: strong induction over all complete regular bases of dimension 2. Steps 2-3: the degree-1 base case and the construction of B = A∩L (normal, finite, complete local, dimension 2, degree drops). Steps 4-5: normalization in K, completed-degree bound, then refinement, completion descent and globalization; hypotheses checked against the statements of the existing nodes. Step 6: separable/degree-p dichotomy; [K:M]=p forces M=F and n=p, R has characteristic p. Steps 7-10: rational model (0B4P), Gorenstein blowups (0BBV), propagation (0BG0), RDP resolution (0BGE), globalization. The new nodes are faithful to their tags. The Gorenstein node replaces 'has a dualizing complex' by 'essentially of finite type over a complete local ring' (implies it by 0BFR) and reads 'ω invertible' as 'Gorenstein local rings', which is correct because normal surfaces are CM. The completed-degree node is true: CM over regular gives flat (00R4), so π is locally free of rank d; completion splits into free factors of rank ≤ d; the completions are normal (0C23); the 'Moreover' clause holds by cancellation of properness. No new node restates a clause of the item; no duplicates found by grep over the snapshot DAG; no SGA citation; the item is still unsplit on live.
